job.title: Software Engineer, Ads
job.pay_full: $165,131 – $229,900 a year base salary, plus equity (restricted stock units)

details.about: Reddit is a community of communities, with more than 100,000 active communities and about 130 million daily active unique visitors. This Software Engineer joins the Ads team, building the backend systems behind Reddit's ad products across creation and serving, and working closely with product, design, frontend, platform and data teams.
duties: Design and build Ads products with product managers, collaborating with the platform and data teams
Build backend systems for ad creation and serving, owning APIs, schema design, data models and storage layers
Design scalable services that support new ad formats, experimentation and long-term platform evolution
Turn ambiguous requirements into clear backend contracts and execution plans with partner teams
Drive migrations, reviews, launches and cross-team technical alignment at production scale
Own service reliability: improve observability, debug production incidents, strengthen test coverage and join on-call rotations
Improve code quality and operational stability, including dashboards and data visualisations
Support project management: updates, timelines and execution
needs: Master's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, any field of Engineering, or a related quantitative discipline
2 years of experience in the job offered or a related occupation
Skills in Go, Python, Scala frameworks, Spark, Thrift, Kafka, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Redis, Kubernetes, Docker, distributed systems and REST APIs
Any suitable combination of education, training and experience is acceptable
details.benefits: Base pay range $165,131 – $229,900 a year (the posting may span more than one career level). The role is also eligible for equity as restricted stock units and, depending on the position, may be eligible for commission. Benefits include comprehensive healthcare and income replacement programs, a 401(k) with employer match, family planning support, mental health and coaching benefits, flexible vacation and paid volunteer time off, and generous paid parental leave.
notes: Apply with a resume and references through the posting (Req. # 1016.344.5)
